To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
γ-irradiating lyophilized poly(lactide co-glycolide (PLG) microparticle formulations for vaccines results in particles that are sterile and retain their potency.

the use of poly(lacti-co-glycolic) polymers with different MWs and γ-irradiating lyophilized PLG formulations for sterilization did not affect the potency of the vaccine formulations for Neisseria meningitis.
γ-irradiations can be used for sterilization of PLG microparticle formulations for vaccines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of sterile PLG formulations for vaccine delivery.
the development of a two-stage strategy for the sterilization of polymeric particles for vaccine delivery by γ-irradianation.
the development of an innovative approach for the sterilization of polymeric particles that can be used as a vaccine delivery system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the γ-irradiations of lyophilized PLG particles does not impair their ability to induce protective immunity.
the use of PLGs with γ-irradiations for vaccine formulation does not impair their immunogenicity.
the γ-irradiating of PLG particles is a feasible and practical method to sterilize the vaccine formulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
γ-irradiating lyophilized PLG formulations is a feasible approach for sterilization and does not impair the vaccine potency.
the PLG particles prepared with γ-irradiations of the lyophilised formulations are equivalent to those produced by the aseptic manufacturing process.
the γ-irradiations of lyophilized PLG formulations do not impair their potency to deliver vaccines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PLG particles prepared using γ-irradiator can be used as a vaccine carrier.
PLG microparticle formulations for vaccines can be sterilized by γ-irradianation without compromising vaccine potency.
the use of PLGs for vaccine formulation is not compromised by the γ-irradiations for sterilization of the PLG formulations.
